audit.whatIsWrong: Three fields say Petricite Burst is charged by Teemo's damage: spikes[0].text "charges off your E poison ticks", early "charges a stored auto off any spell hit — including your E poison tick", whys[0] "detonates off your E poison tick".
audit.why: Riot's own text is "After casting a spell, Sylas stores a charge of Petricite Burst." It charges when SYLAS casts, not when he is hit by a spell. The practical consequence is the opposite of what the entry implies: Teemo cannot avoid arming it by withholding poison, and Sylas always has a charge ready right after any Chain Lash or Kingslayer. The counterplay is the blind, because the charge is spent by a basic attack.
audit.corrected: Petricite Burst arms off Sylas's own casts and is expended by his next basic attack — so every Chain Lash means an empowered auto is loaded, and Blinding Dart is what makes it land on nothing.

audit.whatIsWrong: spikes[1].when is "Lvl 4-5" and its text reads "your shroom radius expands — plant mushrooms at the tribush and river entrances".
audit.why: Noxious Trap is the ultimate — Teemo has no mushrooms at all until level 6. The whole level 4-5 spike is written around an ability that does not exist yet, which sends a player to place wards-that-are-not-there during the one window that is actually pure poke.
audit.corrected: Levels 4-5 are the poke window before mushrooms exist: hold the wave low and punish his walk-ups.

audit.whatIsWrong: whys[2] "Q now max-ranked by level 3"; mid "With Q max-ranked by level 5"; spikes[1].text "Q is max-ranked" at levels 4-5.
audit.why: A champion has 3 skill points at level 3 and 5 at level 5, and Teemo needs points in W and E as well — Q cannot be rank 5 at either level. The emphasis is misplaced regardless: Blinding Dart's cooldown is a flat 7s at every rank, so ranking it up lengthens the blind but never tightens the poke loop the passage is built around.
audit.corrected: Blinding Dart is a flat 7s at all ranks; extra ranks buy blind duration, not a faster loop.

audit.whatIsWrong: The full layer names "Abscond / Abduct" as the matchup-defining cooldown in eight places but never gives a number, and Kingslayer and Hijack timers appear nowhere.
audit.why: The three timers that decide every decision in this lane are Abscond/Abduct 13/12/11/10/9s, Kingslayer 12/10.5/9/7.5/6s and Hijack 80/55/30s. Kingslayer halving from 12s to 6s across the level range is the reason the sustain trade gets worse over time, and it is the number that tells Teemo when trade-and-run stops working.
audit.corrected: Abscond/Abduct 13s at rank 1; Kingslayer 12s at rank 1 falling to 6s maxed; Hijack 80s at rank 1.

audit.why: The Hijack-steals-Noxious-Trap thread (spikes[3], wants.foe[1], whys[4], mid, late) is present and right — a Sylas holding a stolen Noxious Trap can place his own mushrooms, and the entry correctly warns against treating shroom vision as a safe zone. Only the missing 80s timer needed adding.

audit.whatIsWrong: "Blinding Shot" in wants.you[0], early, mid, whys[1].

audit.why: Not a real item name; the full layer for this same matchup already writes Liandry's Torment.

edits.after: Petricite Burst arms whenever SYLAS casts, so every Chain Lash loads an empowered auto — blind him as he steps in and the stored charge lands on nothing.

edits.before: Sylas owns the first two levels in a way most AP tops do not. His passive Petricite Burst charges a stored auto off any spell hit — including your E poison tick — meaning a single auto exchange can detonate a fully empowered burst before you finish walking out. At level 1 that burst plus his Q poke trades roughly even against your AA-poke; at level 2 his W Kingslayer heals a big chunk of what you dealt, erasing the poke lead you thought you banked. Play these first two levels as a farming phase: last-hit at maximum auto range, drop one E poke if he steps up, and save Blinding Shot for the moment he walks in to all-in you rather than spending it on chip.
edits.after: Sylas owns the first two levels in a way most AP tops do not. Petricite Burst arms every time HE casts a spell, so a Chain Lash always comes with an empowered auto loaded — you cannot dodge that by withholding poison, you dodge it by blinding the auto. At level 1 that burst plus his Q poke trades roughly even against your AA-poke; at level 2 his W Kingslayer heals a big chunk of what you dealt, erasing the poke lead you thought you banked. Play these first two levels as a farming phase: last-hit at maximum auto range, drop one E poke if he steps up, and save Blinding Dart for the moment he walks in to all-in you rather than spending it on chip.

edits.before: Level 3 onward the math flips. With Q max-ranked by level 5, Blinding Shot makes his Petricite Burst autos miss on the way in — he burned his E chain to close the gap and his primary auto-reset is wasted. Trade pattern: bait his E1 shield by stepping up slightly, then immediately blind as E2 chain pulls — his follow-up autos miss while your poison runs. Shroom the tribush and river bush entrances so he cannot approach from off-angles, and freeze the wave near your tower to make him overextend for every CS. At level 6 he can steal your R, so note his R cooldown visually before each all-in — a Sylas holding stolen Noxious Trap means the jungle path you assumed was warded is not necessarily safe for him to step into either, but never treat shrooms as CC that stops his dash.
edits.after: Level 3 onward the math flips. Blinding Dart runs on a flat 7s at every rank, so the loop never gets faster — extra ranks just buy blind duration, and that is enough to make his Petricite Burst autos miss on the way in after he has burned his E chain to close. Trade pattern: bait his E1 dash by stepping up slightly, then blind as E2 chain pulls — his follow-up autos whiff while your poison runs. Shroom the tribush and river bush entrances so he cannot approach from off-angles, and freeze the wave near your tower to make him overextend for every CS. At level 6 he can steal your R, so track his Hijack — 80s at rank 1 — before every all-in, and remember a Sylas holding your stolen mushrooms makes your own shroom vision unreliable. Never treat shrooms as CC that stops his dash.

edits.before: Sylas's passive Petricite Burst detonates off your E poison tick and his Q poke deals roughly even damage before your blind is meaningful — farm safe and do not force a 1-for-1 auto trade.
edits.after: Sylas's Petricite Burst arms whenever he casts a spell, so his Chain Lash poke always arrives with an empowered auto attached — farm safe at max range and refuse the 1-for-1 auto trade.

edits.before: His W Kingslayer heals a significant portion of what your E poison dealt, erasing the small level-1 chip lead — stay at max range and hold Blinding Shot for an all-in rather than blowing it on poke.
edits.after: His W Kingslayer heals back much of what your E poison dealt, on a 12s cooldown at rank 1 — stay at max range and hold Blinding Dart for the all-in rather than spending it on chip poke.

edits.before: Q now max-ranked by level 3 makes his E-dash all-in high-risk: blind as he recast-pulls, his empowered autos miss, and your full E poison stack runs while he takes the damage with no heal yet.
edits.after: Blinding Dart at rank 3 already makes his E-dash all-in high-risk: blind as he recast-pulls, his empowered autos whiff, and your full E poison stack runs while Kingslayer is still on cooldown.

edits.before: Q-blind erases his auto-trade window entirely. Only take the trade when Sylas's Abscond / Abduct is down.
edits.after: Blind him and the stored Petricite Burst auto lands on nothing. Trade when Abscond / Abduct is down.

edits.before: - Sylas Abscond / Abduct: matchup-defining — His dash + stun (recast pull). Bait it, then commit. Track it before every engage. - Your committal tool: never spend it on chip. - Your ultimate: the win condition — kill windows only.
edits.after: - Sylas Abscond / Abduct: matchup-defining — 13s at rank 1, his dash, and the recast pulls. Bait it, then commit. - Kingslayer: his heal, 12s at rank 1 down to 6s maxed. - Hijack: 80s, and it takes your Noxious Trap.
